chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the least (recitation in) the Qunut, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Five Glorifications'.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of Qunut recitation required in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the minimum threshold for Qunut as five glorifications, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that brevity suffices unless a specific duration is mandated. This ruling underscores the flexibility within obligatory prayers, allowing worshippers to maintain devotion without undue burden, a concept supported by the Quranic emphasis on ease in worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the least (recitation in) the Qunut. So heasws said: ‘Five Glorifications’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “
I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the minimum form of al-Qunut. He said, ‘It is five times saying, “Allah is free of all defects.’””
